IT infrastructure · 4 min read

A practical starting point for planning an IT infrastructure upgrade

A current-environment review can turn an upgrade into a more manageable business decision.

Start with business needs rather than a shopping list. Identify which work the current environment supports, what has become unreliable and what may change over the next few years.

What to consider

Build an inventory of key systems, equipment, software versions, dependencies and support arrangements. Include the people who rely on those systems. A short inventory can reveal compatibility risks before they delay a project.

Compare options against capacity, recovery, security, administration and lifecycle cost. Consider what can stay, what must change and what needs to integrate with existing services.

Agree on implementation stages, testing, rollback considerations and handover. A phased plan with defined scope makes decisions, dependencies and next steps clearer.
